items.item_text: Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Six (6) years of related experience, education/training, OR a Bachelor’s degree in related area plus two years of related experience/training.
Event planning experience, including vendors, budgets and logistics.

The Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery at UC San Diego Health provides comprehensive clinical care, education and research for disorders of the ear, nose, throat, head and neck. The department has approximately 40 faculty physicians and scientists plus advanced practice providers. It is organized into divisions that include Otology/Neurotology, Laryngology, Rhinology and Skull Base Surgery, Head and Neck Surgical Oncology, Pediatric Otolaryngology, Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, General Otolaryngology, Researchand Audiology. Faculty practice across UC San Diego Health, Moores Cancer Center, Rady Children's Hospital and the VA San Diego Healthcare System. The department also trains residents and fellows and runs a research program that includes NIH-funded training through an R25 program.

The Department Business Office, led by the Department Business Officer, supports the Chair, faculty, trainees and staff. Its work covers academic personnel and human resources, finance, faculty scheduling and timekeeping, events and day-to-day department operations

Under the direction of the Administrative Officer 3 (Academic HR & Personnel Officer), the incumbent provides administrative support to faculty, providers and researchers in assigned divisions of the Department of Otolaryngology / Head and Neck Surgery. Support includes calendaring and meetings, Medical Staff and license renewals, academic reviews, Concur travel and reimbursements, IT, ordering, SPA quarterly reporting and student worker hiring. The incumbent owns department special events from planning through completion, including ENT Nights, special lectures, Research Day and other department events, and creates standard operating procedures (SOPs), timelines and checklists for each event. The incumbent also coordinates observer ship and volunteer appointments, new faculty relocation, the yearly CAMS equipment inventory validation and department mail, and supports the department's R25 program.The incumbent performs other duties and business office needs as assigned. This position requires strong organization, attention to detail,initiative and the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; ability to manage multiple deadlines and recurring cycles.
Familiarity with grant-funded training programs (such as NIH R25).
Calendar and schedule management skills; ability to coordinate meetings across multiple sites and stakeholders.
Solid written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with faculty, staff, vendors and centraloffices.
Ability to own processes and events from start to finish and to document them in clear standard operating procedures.
Working knowledge of UC business systems such as Concur and purchasing systems, and of spreadsheet tools for tracking and reporting.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Ability to take initiative, solve problems and work independently.
